This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 23-07-2021 at about 7.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 from Chandapura, on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, as a pillion rider, being ridden by its rider carefully, cautiously, by following all the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, a Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from behind and dashed against the scooter bearing Reg. No.TN-24-AB-3750 and then to the scooter of the petitioner.

Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/
2 sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient.
Earlier to the accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Sarjapura Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said car, for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.

The respondent No.1 is the driver,
respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 to 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondents No.1 and 2 in their written statement have denied all the allegations made in the petition.

They have contended that, as on the date of alleged accident, the Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 was having valid insurance with the respondent No.3 insurance company,
bundled long term liability policy vide policy No.991491823740007118, valid from 15-10-2020 to 14-10- 2021.
Further they have contended that, as on the date of accident, the driver of said car was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition against them.
5. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of private car/third party liability only policy bearing No.991401823740007118 in favour of respondent No.2, in respect of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05- MY-5409 and it was valid from 15-10-2018 to 14-10-2021 and it was valid as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provisions under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EQ- 0492 which involved in the alleged accident are not made as parties to the above proceedings.
They are the proper and necessary parties to the above proceedings to adjudicate the controversy involved between the parties in the above matter.
It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and also involvement of the vehicle bearing No.KA-05-MY- 5409 as alleged in the claim petition.

Further it is contended that, the respondent No.2 had willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident.
It is clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492, on which the petitioner was the pillion rider.
The rider and pillion riders who were not wearing safety headgear, was not holding driving licence to ride the said motorcycle and insurance to use the said vehicle on the public road.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Further, it has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/
3 Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For the above stated denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 23-07-2021, at about 7.00 p.m., due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Toyota Innova Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY- 5409 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
7.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Further, he has got examined one more witness namely Dr. S.
Ramachandra as P.W.2.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3.
The respondents No.1 and 3 have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

9. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: It is specific case of the petitioner that, on 23-07-2021 at about 7.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding on the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, as a pillion rider, the same being ridden by its rider carefully, cautiously, by following all the traffic rules and regulations.

At that time, the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 5409, drove the same with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from behind and dashed against scooter bearing Reg. No.TN-24- AB-3750 and then to the scooter of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Further it is contended that, earlier to the accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.

4 11.
In order to prove his case, the petitioner has examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of his oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked total 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is certified copy of first information statement, Ex.P.2 is certified copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.3 is certified copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is certified copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.5 is certified copy of Motor Vehicles Accident report, Ex.P.6 is certified copy of reply to notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act, Ex.P.7 is certified copy of post-mortem report, Ex.P.8 is lab report, Ex.P.9 is radiology report with C.D., Ex.P.10 is certified copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.11 are x-rays (total 4), Ex.P.12 is notarized copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner,
Ex.P.13 are medical bills (total 22), Ex.P.14 is OPD record, Ex.P.15 is disability calculation sheet,
Ex.P.16 is x-ray and Ex.P.17 is computer generated discharge summary.
12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7 and 10,
prima -

facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and dashing the same to the motorcycle of the petitioner, from behind.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.4, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409.
13.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 in the said accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.3 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident
, are not in dispute.
But, the respondent No.1 to 3 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident.

Further, the respondent No.3 has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492, on which the petitioner was a pillion rider and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409.
But, the respondent No.3 has failed to establish the said contentions.
Except the self serving statements of the R.W.1/respondent No.2, who is none other than the owner of offending car bearing Reg.

, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 5409 and dashing the same to the scooter bearing Reg.
from behind and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries all over the body in the said accident.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-53-EQ-0492 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/
5 14.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on 42 feet wide of Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, in between the offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY- 5409, scooter bearing No.TN-24-AB-3750 and the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-EQ-0492 of the petitioner, which were proceeding in the same direction.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.4 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.

15. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.8 lab report, Ex.P.9 radiology report with C.D.,
Ex.P.10 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 x-rays (total 4), Ex.P.14 OPD record, Ex.P.15 disability calculation sheet, Ex.P.16 x-ray and Ex.P.17 discharge summary, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained fracture of shaft left humerus.
The same is deposed by P.W.2, who is the doctor who has clinically examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondent No.3, to show that the above medical records are false documents.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.

16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."

17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, " in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/
6 applied."

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident, occurred on 23-07-2021 at about 7:00 p.m., on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, in front of Chambenahalli Gate, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg.
. Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained fracture of shaft left humerus and for the said injury he has undergone surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non- pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
As per Ex.P.12, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1992.
The accident has taken place on 23-07-2021 at about 7:00 p.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 30 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered fracture of shaft left humerus.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, there is 31.32% physical disability of left upper limb and 10.44% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.8 lab report, Ex.P.9 radiology report with C.D., Ex.P.10 wound certificate, Ex.P.11 x-rays (total 4), Ex.P.14 OPD record, Ex.P.15 disability calculation sheet, Ex.P.16 x-ray and Ex.P.17 discharge summary clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and he has undergone surgery for the said injuries.

Though,
the learned counsel for respondent No.3 has cross- examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 23-07-2021 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 31-07-2025, which is after lapse of four years from the date of injuries caused to Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/
7 the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.2 has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the fracture sustained by the petitioner is united and implants are removed,
there are no complications at the operated portion, the external wounds are healed, wrist and elbow joint movements are normal, the loss of movement at shoulder joint is 5.55% and he has assessed only physical disability of the petitioner and not functional disability.

Therefore in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
a) The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2021.

Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,000/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,80,000/-.
b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 30 years is 17.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,80,000 X 8/100 X 17 = Rs.2,44,800/-.
ii) Medical expenses:

The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,70,000/-
towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc.
In order to prove the same, he has produced 22 medical bills, as per Ex.P.13.
All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the bills at serial No.3, 4, 6 and 7 are deposit receipts.
The bills at serial No.11 and 16 are advance receipts.
The bills at serial No.11, 16 and 21 are already included in bill at serial No.14.
Therefore, the said bills are not taken into consideration.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,01,781/- under the head of medical expenses.
iii) Pain and sufferings:

In the present case, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries i.e.
fracture of shaft left humerus.
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days from 23-07-2021 to 26-07-2021, in Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru.
Further, as per P.W.2, the said injuries have caused physical disability to the petitioner.
In such circumstances, certainly the petitioner would have suffered pain and sufferings.

Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.

8 iv)
Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 4 = Rs.4,000/-
is awarded towards the attendant charges.
v) Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.17 discharge summary, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 4 days in Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru.
He might have spent some amount towards food and nourishment during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 4 =
Rs.3,200/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
vi) Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Vijayanagar, Whitefield, Bengaluru, the accident has occurred on Sarjapura-Bengaluru main road, infront of Chambenahalli Gate, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk and he has taken treatment at Columbia Asia Hospital, Bengaluru.
Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places, compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
vii) Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 4 days as in-patient at Columbia Hospital, Bengaluru, for the grievous injuries sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.
Therefore, Rs.15,000 x 2 = Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
viii) Loss of amenities:
It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 30 years and unfortunately he has suffered fracture of shaft left humerus.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 8% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
ix) Future medical expenses:
There is no evidence on record to show that, the petitioner requires any further treatment for the injury sustained in the said accident.
Even, the P.W.2 has not stated anything with respect to same.
Further, the P.W.2 has clearly deposed that, the fracture is united and implants are removed.
In such circumstances, the question of awarding future medical expenses does not arise at all.
Therefore, no compensation is awarded in this particular head.

20. Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads as follows:
1. Loss of future income Rs. 2,44,800-00 2.
Medical expenses 1,01,781-00 3. Pain and sufferings 50,000-00
4. Attendant charges 4,000-00 5.

Food and nourishment 3,200-00 Sathyendra vs Raghavendra H.M on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118684947/
9 6.
Conveyance expenses 10,000-00 7. Loss of income during 30,000-00 treatment period
8. Loss of amenities 30,000-00 9.
Future medical expenses Nil
In all, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,73,781/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
21. Liability:

Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409.

As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy, the policy bearing No.991491823740007118 issued by the respondent No.3 in respect offending Toyota Innova Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409 was valid from 15-10- 2018 to 14-10-2021.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Further as per Ex.R.1, the respondent No.1, who was the driver of the offending vehicle, was holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1/driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,73,781/-
from the respondent No.3, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
22. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.4,73,781/- (Rupees four lakh seventy three thousand seven hundred and eighty one only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioner.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.3 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order.

Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.5, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.4 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondent No.3 has failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Toyota Innova car bearing Reg. No.KA-05-MY-5409 and injuries sustained to the petitioner in the said accident.
16. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
Therefore in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 8% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
Further, he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.3 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, he has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as painter and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident took place in 2021.
Therefore, taking into considering the injuries sustained and disability to the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.1/driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-MY-5409 the accident has occurred and the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
